name: 1901 Prairie Avenue — Norman B. Ream house

grade.why: Pictured: 5 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The 1893 plate, the 1898 photograph and the undated exterior view draw the same composition, the post-1887 rebuilding; nothing read so far records an alteration before 1904.

placement.position_note: The main body's rear north corner: lot frame u 22.83, v -10.20 (the draft's frame point u -1.67, v -0.70 through its own rotation), where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1901-b1) runs the north wall (local y -3322.9) and the stone main body's rear wall north of the brick rear (local x 1444.7). The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation 179.444 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1901 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1901 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The stone main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1901-b1) in the house's frame (u toward the street from the rear wall at local x 1444.7, v south from the north wall at local y -3322.9): the front at local x 1422.3 (u 22.4) and the south wall at y -3338.1 (v 15.2). The sheet's porch box, its flank bays and its brick rear stand on it as K01's door hood, K08 bays and a K01 rear wing; its small chamfer at the south-west corner is drawn smaller than the photographs' cut, which form.cant_corner builds (about 1.83 m each way); the polygon stays the sheet's square trace.

stories.note: Two wall storeys over a raised basement under a dormered mansard, in both Chicagology photographs; the 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the mansard as the third storey.

construction.note: An all-stone house on K01: both photographs show the same light ashlar on the front and the south flank, and the 1911 sheet colours the house stone ('3B', blue). The sheet's brick rear (a pink strip along the east wall, which no picture shows) stands as K01's brick rear wing behind it.

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor about 2.35 m over the house's grade through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the porch's floor at the stoop's head reads about 1.0 m over the base course's top (y 515 against 553 px), and the basement windows' foot (about y 598 px) puts the grade about 1.45 m under that course.

storey_heights_m.note: The principal storey 4.5 m and the chamber storey 3.9 m, to a wall head at 10.8 m through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the principal windows' heads at about 5.6-6.0 m, the chamber windows' sills at about 7.0-7.5 m and heads at about 9.0-9.7 m, and the cornice's bed at about 10.6-10.9 m (the north and south window columns read about 0.6 m apart, the camera's own spread).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front's thickness inside the K01 contract's range; no picture shows a reveal deep enough to read one.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: The flanks are faced in the same stone as the front in both photographs, so they take the front's thickness; no picture reads it.

service_wall_brick.note: The K03 panel K01 keeps for what it lays in brick; on an all-stone house the stone's coursing covers every face. Which brick is reconstruction.

stone_front.note: Smooth light ashlar laid in even courses on the front and the south flank, two deeper courses under the principal floor, in both Chicagology photographs. Which limestone is reconstruction: the prints say only light and smooth; K02's Bedford stone as 1823's.

street_front_trim.note: Every street window under a moulded head with a small cornice on consoles, in both storeys, in both photographs; K09's lintel with a cornice hood. The consoles' carving is the kit's.

wall_head.note: A deep cornice over a frieze at the wall head, carried round the front and both flanks, in both photographs (the exterior view shows it turning the south-west corner and running the south flank's whole length). K10's moulded stone cornice. T-3186: enlarged, both prints show under its corona a course of carved stone blocks, scrolled consoles each with a squared head, single and at an even spacing with dark panels between them, standing on a plain frieze whose foot is a moulded band just over the chamber windows' heads; the earlier reading of them as paired is not what the enlargements show. Built as K10's scrolled console in the walls' stone, its top under the corona's soffit, 0.45 m high and 0.18 m wide, about 0.8 m apart (in the 1898 front view about 23 px apart at about 3.7 cm a pixel along the foreshortened front, and about 17 px high at about 2.7 cm), and the frieze 0.42 m under the cornice's foot, the most the chamber heads leave under it: the pictures read the frieze and blocks together about 0.6-0.8 m high from the band to the corona, and the build's band-to-corona is 0.57 m. The blocks' projection (0.19 m) is the most the corona's soffit covers, and their carving is the kit's generic scroll.

roof_form.note: A slated mansard with dormers over the front and the south flank, in both photographs.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The mansard's upper deck, above every view's sight line.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice stands about 0.5-0.6 m past the front through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json) (the corner block at x 128-152 px over the north corner).

roof_covering.note: Slate on the mansard's faces in both photographs; the deck above the sight line in K04's painted tin.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06's two-over-two flat sash and area lights. The photographs show tall single sash under blinds; the glazing pattern is not readable at their scale.

rainwater.note: K01's copper gutter and two downpipes, both out of the street front's sight; no picture shows them.

stair_tread_m.note: The stoop's treads; the photographs show the flight end-on between its cheeks.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's floor at the stoop's head, about 2.0 m out from the wall through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the porch's front columns stand about 2 m before the front (the sheet's one-storey box is 2.2 m deep).

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop runs between the porch's paired columns, about 2.6 m between its cheeks through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json).

door_clear_height_m.note: The door about 2.45 m clear, under the porch's entablature through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the entablature's foot reads about 5.1 m over grade, so the door's head stands lower than the principal windows' beside it.

entrance_bay.note: The door in the porch, in the front's middle window column between the north part's column and the south part's, in both photographs. K01 counts its bays from the front's north end (its 'south').

front_bays.note: The front's three window columns through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the north part's at x 200-235 px (v 2.65 m), the porch's door and the window over it at x 320-355 px (v about 6.6 m), and the south part's at x 455-500 px (v 11.7 m). The fourth column, on the canted south-west corner the photographs show, is not built (the match record).

sash_by_storey.note: The principal windows about 1.15-1.2 x 3.0 m (K01's widest sash, 1.15 m) and the chamber windows about 1.1 x 2.1 m through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): the south part's principal window x 455-500 px between sill y 505 and head y 402, its chamber window between y 350 and 275.

basement_lights.note: Basement windows under each principal window, about as wide as the sash above, behind the area fence in both photographs.

side_bays.note: The north flank's windows west of its two-storey box (K01's 'south' wall, its s from the rear); no picture shows the north flank, which faces 1827's south flank across a narrow side yard.

north_bays.note: The south flank's windows between the front and its canted bay (K01's 'north' wall, its s from the front): the exterior photograph shows two narrow window columns there in the chamber storey and a small light in the principal storey; K01 lays one window column each at their places. Their narrow width is the match record's. The first column stands at s 2.65, 0.25 m further back than first read, so its jamb clears the canted corner's cut (1.83 m) by the 0.2 m pier K01 keeps; the print places it just past the canted face (x 1200-1260 px), within the camera's spread.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall's window north of the brick rear range; no picture shows the rear.

chimneys.note: Two tall stone stacks on the south flank, one near its front corner and one just east of the dormer over the canted bay, rising over the mansard's curb in the exterior photograph, laid in the walls' own pale ashlar to the cap. Their places are read through that photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_exterior_southwest.json): the front stack's shaft at x 1110-1180 px (u about 19.7) and the rear one's at x 1455-1500 px (u about 9.6), both on the cornice over the side wall; their heights are its proportions, not measured.

entrance_kit.note: The stone porch (portico) on columns over the stoop, its flat top a balcony with a balustrade before the window over the door, in both photographs through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json): about 4.4 m wide (the 1911 sheet's one-storey stone box is 4.4 m by 2.2 m), its entablature from about 5.1 to 5.8 m and its balustrade to about 6.7 m over grade. K01's columned door hood carries it in stone, on two pairs of columns at its front corners (the photographs' paired Corinthian shafts, set 0.75 m apart where K01 keeps their plinths 0.3 m clear and the print sets them about 0.5 m apart centre to centre, under the 1 ft bar), each capital carved as two tiers of leaves under a 0.1 m abacus (T-3186: through the 1898 photograph's camera, at about 2.7 cm a pixel on the shafts, the capitals read about 0.45 m deep with their abacus and about 0.5 m across the leaves; the leafage itself, its volutes and its acanthus, is finer than the print resolves and is not modelled leaf by leaf) with responds at the wall, over stone terraces either side of the stoop at the landing's height, as 1729's portico stands. The stoop's two cheeks are K07's scrolled stone cheek (T-3186): the print draws each as a solid stone wall sweeping down in a concave curve from the inner column's foot at the landing's edge to a roll lying across it at the flight's foot; the south-west view shows its moulded top running straight down the rake to the roll (its midpoint on the chord from head to foot, read at three times the print's pixels), so the sweep falls straight (bow 1), not in the concave fall a scrolled cheek otherwise takes. The print also cuts a row of small openings along each cheek under its top, which K07's scrolled cheek does not build (the match records). The front 9.35 m behind the street line (the sheet). WHERE: the photographs put the porch's columns at v about 5.3 and 9.0 m, about 1.5 m north of where the sheet draws its box (v 6.5-10.8); three pictures agree and the build follows them (docs/LIBERTIES.md).

boundary.note: A low iron fence on a stone curb along the street line, its panels a band of C-scrolls under the top rail, with tall square stone posts at its gates and at the south corner, in both photographs: K11's scroll-band fence on the kit's stone piers. The scrolls' exact pattern (the prints draw paired loops) is the kit's. The lot's sides are the 1904 parcel's (data/street_grid/1904.json); the fence's line 9.1 m before the front, its curb's face on the sheet's street line (9.35 m). T-3206: the entrance pair is drawn standing open into the yard, 70 degrees, so the walk's way in reads open from the street (reconstructed: no picture shows the leaves' state; liberty L-k14-walks-1800-block-3206).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the canted bay's cheek lights, one a storey on its west cheek in both photographs (the 1898 one at x 735-765 px)
the bay's front lights, two a storey; the exterior photograph shows the front's west light
the cheek's chamber light over the principal one, in both photographs
the box's principal-storey lights, reconstructed: no picture shows the north flank

bays.note: Two K08 bays on the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1901-b1) in the house's frame (u toward Prairie Avenue from the rear wall, v south from the north wall): the south flank's canted bay, 8.85 m along the wall from 8.35 to 17.2 m behind the front and 1.9 m out on the sheet (1.8 m built, K08's deepest), in the front's stone and carried through both storeys under the cornice in both photographs (its west cheek and front lights as they draw them; its cants made even, 1.43 m, where the sheet draws 1.65 and 1.2); and the north flank's box, 7.4 m long and 1.6 m out ('2B' on the sheet), whose openings no picture shows (reconstruction).

mansard.note: The slated mansard rising about 4.5 m over the wall head to its curb through the 1898 photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_1898_front.json) (the deck's cresting at about y 100 px over the north part reads 14-15.5 m over grade), K05's most for a one-storey face; its faces steep and nearly straight. Three street dormers over the three window columns under pedimented heads, the middle one the largest, and an iron cresting along the curb, in both photographs. Their pediments low and triangular, about 30 deg (the kit's lowest), in the south-west view. A fourth dormer stands on the south flank's face over the canted bay's west end (K01's north face, 11.2 m from the rear wall), pedimented as the street's are, in the exterior photograph (x 1380-1450 px, read through its camera at about u 11.2, data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_exterior_southwest.json). A fifth stands on the canted south-west corner's face over its window column (face 'cant'), the largest of the front's in the 1898 photograph and pedimented as the others in the south-west one (its face about x 950-1115 px with its carved cheeks, its sash about x 995-1065 px, about 1.0 m by 1.9 m through that camera); K01 lays it at the middle street dormer's size, centred on the canted face's lower slope.

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's brick rear: the east wall stands 3.1 m further back south of v 5.6 (lot x 1444.7-1447.8 on the trace), coloured brick, at the main body's height; on K01's rear wings, laid in K03 brick, under a flat roof. Its windows are reconstruction: no picture shows the rear.

cant_corner.note: The front's south-west corner (K01's 'north') cut on a canted face square to the corner, from the base course to the mansard's curb, with its own window column on both storeys, in both photographs. The south-west photograph's camera (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/chicagology_exterior_southwest.json) fits the cut about 1.83 m back each way, its face about 2.6 m across between x 942 and 1120 px; the 1898 camera's weaker fit reads about 2.5 m and the 1911 sheet draws a smaller chamfer. K01 lays the face in the front's ashlar on its beds, a window at its middle in each storey at the storey's sash and a basement light under them (the print shows the column; the basement light is the front's, reasoned from the lights under every principal window), and carries the moulded cornice, the mansard's faces, the gutter and the curb's cresting round it.

grade_m.note: the app's ground over the house's lowest foot, measured in the published 1904 app (T-3206): the yard is lifted onto it so the lawn and the walk are not under it

yard.note: T-3206 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The walk in flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate to the public walk; the cinder service walk from the side gate down the north passage to the house's rear corner. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1800-block-3206.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone with brick rear dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped); Norman B. Ream's house in the 1898 photograph's caption and the 1893 Pictorial Chicago plate.

citations.citation: 1901 S. Prairie Ave. 'In 1898 as owned by Mr. Ream.' [Norman B. Ream house, from across Prairie Avenue to the south-west.] Unknown photographer, 1898 (the hosting page's caption). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1901 S. Prairie.

the heights of the principal floor, both storeys, the windows, the porch and the mansard through the photograph's camera
the tone of the walls: a light smooth stone

the south flank's rear half, behind the canted bay

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2330) in place by T-3185 (piece 1 of T-1903), under the draft's own id, as a K01 stone-front house read off the 1898 Chicagology photograph of Norman B. Ream's house (chicagology_1901_ream_1898) and the undated exterior view (chicagology_1901_ream_exterior) against the 1911 sheet's plan: the smooth ashlar front block two storeys over a raised basement under a slated, dormered mansard and a deep blocked cornice; the porch on columns at the stoop's head with its balustraded balcony over the door; the south flank's canted bay and the north flank's box; the brick rear; an iron fence on a stone curb. The 1898 photograph's camera and match record are in data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/; what the pictures show that is not built yet (the canted south-west corner, the porch's paired Corinthian columns and curved stoop cheeks, the flank dormers) is open there for T-3186.
